top_stories.title: Vande Bharat Sleeper train: RVNL targets December 2026 for first prototype launch
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL)** has revised the timeline for the rollout of its first Vande Bharat Sleeper prototype to December 2026, pushing back the initial June 2026 target. The project, valued at approximately Rs 14,400 crore, will see **Kinet Railway Solutions**, a joint venture between **TMH** and **RVNL**, manufacture 16-coach trains with 35 years of maintenance arrangement.  The Ministry of Railways awarded the contract to three companies: BEML, Kinet Railway Solutions, and a consortium of Titagarh Rail Systems Limited and Bharat Heavy Engineering Limited (BHEL).

top_stories.title: Mamata Banerjee meets Kejriwal ahead of INDIA bloc meeting - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, chief of the **Trinamool Congress**, met with **Arvind Kejriwal**, convener of the **Aam Aadmi Party**, in Delhi on Sunday. The meeting, described as "warm," focused on the future direction of the opposition bloc **INDIA**.  The two leaders discussed the road ahead for the group, which will meet on Monday to strategize against the BJP and address differences arising from recent Assembly election results.

top_stories.title: Early warning bells for AAP in Punjab? Why groups that powered its 2022 win are protesting | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Bhagwant Mann**'s Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab is facing growing discontent from various groups, including government employees, contractual workers, and unemployed youth. Protests have intensified over pending demands for jobs, wages, promotions, dearness allowance (DA), and pension benefits.  The PSPCL apprenticeship linemen union has been protesting outside the headquarters of the power corporations, while thousands of outsourced Sewa Kendra employees are on strike demanding enhanced wages. The Berozgar Sanjha Morcha has also staged a prolonged dharna demanding government job reforms, including an increase in the upper age limit for recruitment and more opportunities.  The protests have drawn criticism from the Opposition parties, who accuse the AAP government of failing to fulfill its election promises.

top_stories.title: Encounter actions in U.P. undermine criminal justice system, make society barbaric: Former police officers - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: Retired **DGP-rank officials** from the Uttar Pradesh cadre expressed concern over the state government's release of data on police encounters, stating that it has "made society barbaric" and negatively impacted democratic growth. They argued that this policy fosters a culture of lawlessness and undermines the criminal justice system, drawing parallels to past campaigns like the "Maro, Maro" campaign during the V.P. Singh regime.

top_stories.title: Blue economy offers unlimited opportunities for ‘Puthuyuga Keralam’: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** emphasized the importance of sustainable development, responsible maritime governance, and conservation for Kerala's 600-kilometer coastline.  He highlighted this as a key focus for the state's economic growth, particularly in light of the upcoming World Oceans Day on June 8th. **The UDF government**, with its "Dream Project" (Mission Samudra), aims to transform Kerala into a global maritime hub.

top_stories.title: Beyond remittances: Why experts say Bihar can no longer rely solely on exporting its labour | Patna News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Former Chief Justice Sanjay Kumar**, while delivering the keynote address at **Grand Trunk Road Initiatives (GTRI)** 6.0, emphasized the importance of institutional trust, governance, and law and order for economic development.  Delegates discussed Bihar's financial architecture, migration patterns, and dependence on external revenue sources. They highlighted the need for stronger institutions, increased investment, and large-scale industrialization to convert human resources into sustainable economic growth. The conference also addressed technology, financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, and the role of artificial intelligence in boosting Bihar's economy.  Delegates concluded that sustained economic transformation requires coordinated efforts across government, industry, and civil society.

top_stories.title: 22-year-old student shot dead after chasing phone robbers in Philadelphia; father says, 'I'm shocked he went after them' - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A 22-year-old Penn State student, **Billy Schmidt**, was fatally shot in Philadelphia early Saturday morning after trying to retrieve his stolen phone. Surveillance footage showed **Schmidt** confronting the suspects before being shot, and he died from his injuries at Penn Presbyterian Medical Center.  Police have not announced any arrests in the ongoing investigation. The incident has shocked residents who are struggling to understand how a dispute over a phone could lead to such tragedy.

top_stories.title: Expert Explains | Why AI Growth Narratives Hide Labour Costs in India
top_stories.rephrased_article: The "AI Resist List" documents global efforts to challenge the influence of AI across areas like labor, data extraction, and surveillance.  **Petra Molnar**, a lawyer and anthropologist, highlights how narratives framing AI as a pathway to economic growth often obscure questions of labor, infrastructure, and democratic accountability. **India**, for example, appears across all pillars of AI power, highlighting the extractive nature of this technology. The list reveals that AI power is assembled through unequal relationships with global supply chains and extraction of cognitive labor from the Global Majority.  Communities and policymakers should demand binding commitments, independent assessments of environmental and social impacts, and genuine data governance to ensure equitable benefits and prevent erasure of human contributions.

top_stories.title: Israeli soldier guns down 7-month-old Palestinian baby, family questions claims | World News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Sam Fahd Abu Haikal**, a seven-month-old Palestinian baby, was killed in Hebron on Friday after being shot by Israeli soldiers. **The IDF** claims the shooting occurred when troops perceived a vehicle accelerating towards them, but **Fahd Abu Haikal**, the baby's father, and his family dispute this account, stating that the car had stopped before gunfire erupted.  The incident is part of a broader surge in violence across the West Bank since the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023.

top_stories.title: DMK absent, allies restive, INDIA bloc braces for a difficult conversation at today’s meeting | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: The Opposition INDIA bloc is set to meet in Delhi on Monday, facing a weakened position after the recent Assembly elections and internal tensions. The absence of the DMK due to its disagreement with the Congress over the Tamil Nadu government's formation has added to the complexity.  **Mamata Banerjee**, **Abhishek Banerjee**, and other leaders are expected to play a mediating role as the bloc grapples with issues including electoral rolls, delimitation, simultaneous elections, education system concerns, and coordination.
